races.name: Dragon Symbol Standing At Whitsbury Manor British EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Breacher
runners_data.comment: By Cracksman, an outstanding middle-distance performer, out of the smart middle-distance performer Callendula and a half-brother to a useful sprinter; probably effective over today's 7f trip on pedigree, he is an intriguing newcomer and worth following in the market.

runners_data.name: Galipi
runners_data.comment: Encouraged by a debut effort at Ffos Las where he was unsettled early but found his stride in the closing stages, finishing third beaten two lengths; handles good to soft and should benefit from that initial experience, making him an interesting proposition.

runners_data.name: Jiro
runners_data.comment: Overraced early and faded quickly at Newmarket on debut, beaten well back; bred to be effective around 7f and may progress with experience, but he has a lot to find against rivals in this field.

runners_data.name: Power Effort
runners_data.comment: A Good Effort colt whose dam was fair over a mile and a quarter and a half-brother to a useful 8f performer; his trainer is in good heart at present and a market check is worth taking before the off.

runners_data.name: Rafe's Da Man
runners_data.comment: Fourth on debut at Lingfield, beaten a significant distance, but he has the pedigree of a half-brother to a useful all-weather performer at a mile and is expected to move forward from that initial experience.

runners_data.name: See The Mountain
runners_data.comment: A 70,000gns Kameko colt out of a dam who showed her worth over middle distances; from a top trainer with a strong record with juveniles, he merits a market check and should be respected on debut.

runners_data.name: Spruce
runners_data.comment: By Advertise, out of a dam who showed pace at two and a half-brother to a useful 6f performer; likely to need this experience to fully fire, he is one to watch develop with racing.

runners_data.name: Squadron
runners_data.comment: A Frankel colt out of a dam who was sharp over 7f as a juvenile, representing a trainer with an excellent course record — the yard has landed this race twice in the last nine runnings; he looks a likely type and merits a market check.

races.name: Whitsbury Manor Stud Supporting Inspire Foundation Handicap

runners_data.name: King Of Stars
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old hold-up type returning from 273 days off the track under Alistair Rawlinson, whose trainer Michael Appleby has a modest 2/25 14-day strike rate; the lengthy absence combined with a deeply unreliable recent form string (10th, 12th, 4th, 3rd, 7th) makes this a very speculative runner regardless of pace shape, and similar-going figures of just 0W4P from 11 runs offer little optimism.
runners_data.comment: Returning from a lengthy absence and wearing first-time cheekpieces, he was beaten seven lengths at Bath on his comeback; he has shown he enjoys bowling along from the front and is effective over today's trip, though he has more to prove after a modest reappearance.

runners_data.name: The Thames Boatman
runners_data.note: Ran nine days ago and showed a win at 5f on good-to-firm conditions (1W in similar going), but his true racing style is hold-up and he has been mapped into midfield only because there are too many rear-of-field types for the race shape to absorb; Finley Marsh will try to push forward but this horse is unlikely to secure a natural berth and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.93 is a real drag on his prospects here.
runners_data.comment: Won at Goodwood three starts back, looking in good nick for a spell before running far too freely to do himself justice on his latest outing; back on the same mark and adding cheekpieces for the first time, he is capable of better over this trip on any going.

runners_data.name: Silver Wraith
runners_data.note: David Probert's mount is a natural prominent racer with two wins in her last six starts, and the step back to 5f (she has run well at 6f) is the key unknown — her last two 5f runs produced a 7th and a 2nd, with the place on good ground encouraging; Emma Lavelle's team has not fired in the last 14 days (0/8) but the horse's front-rank style and good-to-firm aptitude make her the obvious pace-shape beneficiary.
runners_data.comment: Won at Bath by a short margin three starts back and ran with credit until an off-day in stronger company last time; wearing a first-time tongue-tie and back in softer grade, 1lb below her last winning mark, she looks a live threat on a sound surface.

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Seamus Cronin (5lb claimer) partners this horse who has won twice in five runs with a pattern of strong prominent-to-hold-up finishes, but like The Thames Boatman he is a natural hold-up operator squeezed out of his ideal position by the field's composition; the 0.92 STYLE_FIT flag reflects that he is unlikely to race where he is happiest, and the claim alone does not compensate for the tactical disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: Took a contest at Southwell convincingly three starts back before struggling under a higher mark in a more competitive setting last time; now rated 2lb lower, but his current level remains a concern, though he handles any going and has enough ability to place.

runners_data.name: Fresh Fade
runners_data.note: A three-year-old hold-up type trained by Michael Attwater (0/8 over 14 days) whose recent form of 0,4,5,6,12 is deeply uninspiring; Luke Morris takes over but the horse's best effort on similar going was a win at 5f on standard ground (Southwell), and the Salisbury surface profile looks a step up in class and pace — hard to make a case here.
runners_data.comment: Nowhere near his best in a handicap at Windsor on his most recent outing, failing to find any extra when asked; his form has deteriorated and he is difficult to enthuse about at present, despite being effective on a range of going.

runners_data.name: Connie's Rose
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field and a seven-year-old who has placed five times in 15 runs on similar going; Ray Dawson knows this mare's game and will use the front-running role to control tempo unchallenged, which on this flat 5f track under good-to-firm conditions is a significant structural advantage — headgear (tp) confirms she is kept sharp and her 15-day freshness is ideal for a front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Back to form under an aggressive ride when runner-up at Chepstow last time, a half-length behind after dropping in trip; now fitted with first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces, she is just 1lb above her last winning mark and acts on most turf going.

races.paceDynamic: Connie's Rose is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 5f handicap and, with no other horse genuinely contesting early leadership, she will stride into an uncontested lead from the gate and control every fraction of this race at her own tempo. On good-to-firm ground over the minimum trip at Salisbury, that scenario translates to a true-pace, rail-hugging gallop that is sustainable rather than suicidal — the kind of rhythm that keeps prominent horses honest without blowing them away. Silver Wraith is the natural challenger from a prominent position and is the only runner with an uncomplicated path to the front rank, while The Thames Boatman and Cayman Tai are genuine hold-up types redistributed into the midfield map simply because there are more closers in this field than the race shape can accommodate at the rear. The race shape strongly favours the front-end profile: one leader, one real prominent handler, and a pack of hold-up types who will be hunting ground they may never fully bridge on a flat, fast track where the leader sets a metronomic tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Connie's Rose Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Connie's Rose jumps cleanly and no horse is able to press her early, allowing her to bowl along in front at a controlled but honest clip.
scenarios.body: If Connie's Rose jumps cleanly and no horse is able to press her early, allowing her to bowl along in front at a controlled but honest clip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Challenger Reels In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Silver Wraith travels smoothly in second throughout and finds a gear in the final furlong to wear down Connie's Rose before the line.
scenarios.body: If Silver Wraith travels smoothly in second throughout and finds a gear in the final furlong to wear down Connie's Rose before the line.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to compress the late closers' margins and one of the redistributed hold-up types finds a clear run through a tiring field.
scenarios.body: If the pace is fast enough to compress the late closers' margins and one of the redistributed hold-up types finds a clear run through a tiring field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace, Bunched Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at an unexpectedly conservative tempo that compresses the field and produces a blanket finish where any runner can grab a piece.
scenarios.body: If the race is run at an unexpectedly conservative tempo that compresses the field and produces a blanket finish where any runner can grab a piece.

watchPoints.text: Connie's Rose jumps cleanly — if she misses the break, the entire race shape collapses and the hold-up types suddenly have a genuine chance of meeting a chaotic scramble rather than a controlled pace.

The Thames Boatman and Cayman Tai are genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield; if either tries to push forward early and takes the pace on rather than settling, it could create more pace than Connie's Rose expects and compress the race dramatically.

Silver Wraith's form tails off sharply over 5f (7th on good ground last time at this trip) — if she fails to travel prominently and gets caught in a pocket, her chance evaporates quickly on this flat track with no undulations to help closers.

King Of Stars returns from 273 days off — watch in-running for any signs of rustiness or reluctance to commit; a horse this far off a run can either strip fitter than expected or simply blow up late, and either outcome affects how the back-markers navigate.

races.name: Juddmonte EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Flying Pirate
runners_data.comment: Won a novice here on debut by the narrowest margin, a promising first effort despite greenness and drifting on the undulations; handles soft ground and should take another step forward, making him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Metamouse
runners_data.comment: Stepped up on his debut effort to land a novice at Chester by three lengths last time, showing clear progression on good to soft; effective over today's trip, he takes on this under a penalty, which asks more of him.

runners_data.name: Harry Knows
runners_data.comment: Narrow runner-up in a novice here last time, with his form reading well at a higher level; his dam was effective at a mile and beyond, hinting the trip may suit him better still, and the yard has a strong record at this track.

runners_data.name: Herbert Hall
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way in a novice at Newbury on his only start, he has plenty to do to get involved here; his breeding suggests 6-7f will be his optimum range, but he needs to show considerably more.

runners_data.name: Ten Of Clubs
runners_data.comment: Beaten a long way on debut at Wolverhampton, never getting into contention having been unsettled early; speedily bred but yet to show ability to match that pedigree, and has plenty to find against this field.

runners_data.name: Treasurer
runners_data.comment: Acquitted himself respectably when fourth on debut before stepping up to a Group 2 at Ascot last time, where he was beaten nine lengths; effective over today's trip on a sound surface, he remains open to development and should fare better back in this company.

runners_data.name: Keep Grating
runners_data.comment: A Salisbury debutant by the top-class miler Space Traveller, out of the speedy Secret Liaison and a half-brother to a useful 6f performer; probably effective over today's trip on pedigree, he merits a market check before committing.

runners_data.name: Ten Year Stretch
runners_data.comment: Never threatened in a novice here on debut, dropping away having been left behind early; his mixed sprint and stamina pedigree hints a longer trip may suit him better, and this represents a tough assignment.

runners_data.name: Calendar Boy
runners_data.comment: A Gregorian colt bought for 19,000gns, representing a trainer capable of fielding debut winners with a strong record at this venue; market moves before the off are worth noting.

runners_data.name: Poppy Foxy
runners_data.comment: Showed clear progression when taking a seller at Chester by a length last time, overcoming positional difficulties on the way; her combination of a sprint sire and a stamina-oriented dam suggests she has more to give, though better company awaits.

runners_data.name: Martha Brown
runners_data.comment: Placed third on her most recent outing at Bath, six lengths adrift in a maiden, but has a lot of ground to make up at this level; her breeding points to 6-7f as her likely range, and she returns after a seven-week break.

races.name: Havana Grey Standing At Whitsbury Manor Handicap

runners_data.name: Addison Grey
runners_data.note: Regular 6f performer on good ground with a proven win at this trip in similar conditions (1/6f/GOO in recent hist), travels prominently and suits the expected controlled-pace shape; David Probert and Clive Cox team is in solid 14-day form at 3/17, and 45 days off is not a concern given the horse's course-style suitability.
runners_data.comment: Forced to switch and given too much to do at Newbury last time, so the two-length defeat flatters the task he faced; all his form comes on a sound surface, he acts at six furlongs, and the current mark looks generous.

runners_data.name: Another Abbot
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand partners a William Haggas hold-up horse that won over 6f on good recently, though its last two efforts at 5f were modest and the return to 6f with a prominent field may leave it last or nearly last; cheekpieces (hg:t) noted, and Haggas firing at 12/59 over 14 days is healthy — genuine closer but needs something to go wrong up front to get involved.
runners_data.comment: Won at Yarmouth last time, showing plenty of tenacity to hold on by a head; first-time tongue-tie is added here, the trainer is in fine form, and while the mark has moved up 6lb, there could be more to come from him.

runners_data.name: Jel Pepper
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed pace-setter and highest-rated runner at OR 95, though the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 signals it is somewhat out of character racing in the prominent role it is assigned — its best form (1/7f/GOO) came over further, and its 6f record on good ground is limited (1W from 8 similar-going runs); Lewis Edmunds takes the ride for Oliver Cole, who is in modest 14-day form at 1/8.
runners_data.comment: Given an extremely rough passage at Windsor last time on a trip shorter than ideal, the heavy defeat can be set aside; seven furlongs suits him better and he handles any ground, though the mark he carries may test him at this level.

runners_data.name: Sudden Flight
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes has a lightly tried 4-year-old that won at 6f on standard and placed twice at this trip, but its true running style is prominent and it finds itself with more prominent rivals ahead of it than it would like — it may push forward regardless, which is the key variable in whether this race stays truly steady; recent form on genuine good ground is thin (0W1P in similar going), and the 23-day gap is fine.
runners_data.comment: Narrowly out-battled at Goodwood last time on a mark 1lb below today's, so the form is in the right place; first-time cheekpieces today add interest, and he handles the fast ground at five to six furlongs.

runners_data.name: Egoli
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3-year-old has struggled for a win lately (form reads 6548-9) and its Topspeed figures at 6f on good are unremarkable, but it races prominently and should hold a tracking position behind Jel Pepper; Hector Crouch rides for a trainer firing at 7/57 over 14 days, and the 29-day break is standard — needs career-best to win but is a natural occupant of the prominent slot.
runners_data.comment: Well below par on his handicap debut at Windsor most recently, but his two-year-old form suggested rather more; effective at six furlongs on this going, he is in the hands of a strong operator at this venue and could leave that effort well behind.

runners_data.name: Fleetwater
runners_data.note: David Egan picks up a JS Moore runner that has placed over 6f on standard and soft ground, and whose natural inclination is to race up with the pace — squeezed out of a front position by the density of prominent types in this field, it will need to work hard early to find its spot or settle further back than ideal; the 15-day turnaround is short but the horse has been busy all season, and the STYLE_FIT discount is real.
runners_data.comment: Front-running tactics backfired at Windsor last time, where she was used up early and dropped well away; her earlier form includes a couple of creditable placings at this trip, but our figures have her lowest of the seven runners.

runners_data.name: Queue Dos
runners_data.note: JS Moore's second runner brings 6f place form on good ground (3/6f/GOO in hist) and has genuine pace instincts, but the field's prominent logjam means Joe Leavy will likely find it racing out of its comfort zone in midfield; OR 76 is the lowest in the field, and while it has won at 6f on standard, the step up in class here combined with its likely unfavoured map position makes this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: A clear effort to forget at Lingfield last time on what appeared to be unsuitable soft ground; first-time cheekpieces are added today and she runs off her last winning mark, but her inconsistent profile keeps her at the back of our assessment.

races.paceDynamic: Jel Pepper is the one confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push them hard for the lead, is expected to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over Salisbury's flat six furlongs on good-to-firm ground. Addison Grey and Egoli will track closely in the prominent positions, meaning the pace picture from the front three is orderly rather than pressured. The field actually contains a cluster of natural front-running and prominent types — Sudden Flight, Fleetwater, and Queue Dos are all genuine pace horses who have been redistributed to midfield on the map simply because Jel Pepper, Addison Grey, and Egoli are likely to fill the front positions first; of those three, Sudden Flight is the most likely to push forward and contest position, with Fleetwater and Queue Dos the ones most likely to be shuffled back against their nature. A sustainable, uncontested pace on good-to-firm ground at a flat track heavily favours prominent racers who can travel close to the fractions and quicken from a position of comfort — front-rank types with a proven finishing kick at this trip and going are best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Jel Pepper sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race is decided in the final two furlongs between horses who tracked the fractions.
scenarios.body: If Jel Pepper sets a steady, uncontested pace and the race is decided in the final two furlongs between horses who tracked the fractions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Sudden Flight pushes forward aggressively to contest the lead with Jel Pepper, creating a faster pace that drains the front two.
scenarios.body: If Sudden Flight pushes forward aggressively to contest the lead with Jel Pepper, creating a faster pace that drains the front two.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Jel Pepper produces a career-best front-running display, dictating an even pace and simply outclassing rivals with a decisive kick.
scenarios.body: If Jel Pepper produces a career-best front-running display, dictating an even pace and simply outclassing rivals with a decisive kick.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Redistribution Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple natural prominent types fight for position early and the resulting pace collapse or sprint catches everyone by surprise.
scenarios.body: If the multiple natural prominent types fight for position early and the resulting pace collapse or sprint catches everyone by surprise.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Sudden Flight pushes forward at the break — if it contests the lead with Jel Pepper rather than settling, the pace will quicken meaningfully and change the race shape entirely.

Addison Grey's 45-day absence is the longest layoff in the field; if it needs the run to find full stride, its prominent position could flatter early and fade late on ground that rewards those fully wound up.

Fleetwater and Queue Dos are both JS Moore runners who naturally want to be prominent — monitor their early behaviour to see whether one or both push forward and inadvertently create a more pressured pace than the headline map suggests.

The going report consistently reads Good To Firm for this 6f slot at Salisbury, faster than the declared Good — horses with soft or standard-track form should be assessed against this, particularly Another Abbot (4/5f/STA, 10/6f/STA in recent hist) and Sudden Flight (2/6f/SOF, 14/6f/SOF).

races.name: Madar Corporation EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Paniolo Creek
runners_data.comment: A son of Eastern Anthem whose dam showed limited promise over ten furlongs in France; this looks an educational debut and he enters as the lowest-rated runner in the field.

runners_data.name: Sevenkingsmustdie
runners_data.comment: Finished down the field at Windsor on his Flat debut, but a more testing race may have been what he needed; first-time hood is applied today and the trainer is currently in good form, though making the step up from bumper level takes time.

runners_data.name: Zachary Hickes
runners_data.comment: Beaten 8l at Windsor last time after a below-par effort, but that run should have sharpened him up; bred to get 10f or more and our figures rate him second of the field, though he may ultimately find his level in handicaps.

runners_data.name: Al Qatem
runners_data.comment: Well backed on his debut at Wolverhampton, he was beaten further than his potential suggests and a step up to a longer trip looks exactly what his breeding demands; the first outing can be set aside and he could leave it well behind.

runners_data.name: Storming Point
runners_data.comment: Close second at Windsor on his latest start, beaten only a length, with his debut form since boosted by those he ran against; he acts well on fast ground and rates a colt of genuine potential at the top of our figures.

runners_data.name: Virtue Diligence
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in both starts so far, though he went up in trip at Windsor latest and showed a step forward from his debut; bred for middle distances, he may have more to offer, but the real progress is likely to come in handicap company.

runners_data.name: Aleatrix
runners_data.comment: An unraced daughter of Study Of Man out of Alabelle, herself useful over middle distances; related to Ebury, useful at a mile, she has an attractive pedigree for today's trip and comes from a yard with a strong record placing debutants.

races.name: Showcasing Standing At Whitsbury Manor Bibury Cup Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Gone By
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo front-runner arrives on the back of a win over 11f on Good and has shown the ability to make all effectively; uncontested lead in a three-runner field is a significant tactical gift, and his sim-going record of 1W2P in Good conditions underlines his suitability to today's surface.
runners_data.comment: Demolished her rivals at Ripon last time by a wide margin, drawing clear with authority to take a maiden; debut form has since been given strong endorsement and her opening official mark looks lenient, with a step up to 12 furlongs suiting her profile.

runners_data.name: Pearl River
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's 3yo has a recent win to her name but all five of her last runs have been over 10f, making this 1m4f step up the key question; Joe Leavy takes the ride and she is comfortably placed on the Going, though her stamina for the trip is unproven and she must track a front-runner who will control the tempo.
runners_data.comment: Won a handicap at York on a 6lb lower mark and dropping in class last time; effective at eight to ten furlongs and acts on this going, though his inconsistent profile means more is needed off the revised mark.

runners_data.name: Mythical Valentine
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3yo has shown a consistent profile at 12f, winning and placing over today's trip in recent outings, which gives her the most convincing distance credentials in the field; Callum Hutchinson partners her and she is 36 days fresh, with her sim-going record of 1W2P suggesting she handles this surface, though she must overcome a 9lb pull at the weights versus Gone By.
runners_data.comment: Won a maiden at Windsor last time and has shown a positive trajectory, with his official mark appearing lenient for a horse that stays this trip; the quicker ground today might not bring out his best on turf, which is the main reservation.

races.paceDynamic: Gone By is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of just three and will lead from the outset without any pressure, setting a controlled, measured gallop over Salisbury's 1m4f at Good to Firm. Pearl River and Mythical Valentine are both prominent types who will track closely behind, likely racing in a tight group given the small field, meaning this shapes up as a processional with minimal tactical complexity. The lack of any genuine hold-up horse means there is no late velocity being stored in the rear, and the race will be decided by who sustains best from the front two furlongs out rather than any dramatic finish. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and horses with proven stamina who can race prominently without burning excessive energy — Gone By's ability to dictate an uncontested, even tempo is the defining tactical factor.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gone By Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Gone By bowls along in front at a comfortable gallop and neither trailer has the foot to mount a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: If Gone By bowls along in front at a comfortable gallop and neither trailer has the foot to mount a sustained challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace from Gone By allows Pearl River or Mythical Valentine to travel dangerously close and unleash a finish that overwhelms him.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace from Gone By allows Pearl River or Mythical Valentine to travel dangerously close and unleash a finish that overwhelms him.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Test Breaks Them
scenarios.trigger: If the pace surprisingly quickens mid-race or the ground rides more testing than Good to Firm, exposing stamina limits in the younger trio.
scenarios.body: If the pace surprisingly quickens mid-race or the ground rides more testing than Good to Firm, exposing stamina limits in the younger trio.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pearl River Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If Pearl River travels with unusual ease just off the pace and produces a sharp turn of foot in the final furlong that catches Gone By napping.
scenarios.body: If Pearl River travels with unusual ease just off the pace and produces a sharp turn of foot in the final furlong that catches Gone By napping.

watchPoints.text: Gone By's jockey Hector Crouch must resist any temptation to over-increase the gallop once settled — if he allows Pearl River and Mythical Valentine to coast alongside him for free, the value of his lead entirely evaporates in a three-runner race.

Pearl River's stamina at 1m4f is genuinely untested; if the pace picks up sharply entering the Salisbury straight she may be vulnerable to being outstayed, and backers should note she has not run beyond 10f in any of her five career starts.

Mythical Valentine's 9lb lower weight versus Gone By is a meaningful edge in a small-field handicap — if the race develops into a true stamina test in the closing stages, that weight allowance could prove decisive.

With only three runners, race dynamics are unusually transparent — watch whether Pearl River and Mythical Valentine sit together just off Gone By or whether one of them attempts to challenge for second gear early, which would be a tell for how the finish develops.

The Going Report confirms 1m4f as Good to Firm at Salisbury today, identical to the stated Going — no hidden deterioration expected, and all three runners are flagged OK on going, meaning conditions create no meaningful differentiation between the field.

races.name: Molson Coors Handicap

runners_data.name: Hot And Cold
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott plots his horses meticulously and this filly returns after 224 days off having won at Lingfield last time; she holds the confirmed lead role here and Good to Firm suits, though racing as a prominent type slightly outside her mapped position is a minor caveat.
runners_data.comment: Won a novice at Newcastle on a drop in trip last time, and her middle-distance breeding points to more in handicap company at three; the lengthy absence since is the one risk to weigh.

runners_data.name: Dark Sovereign
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's in-form yard (7/57 over 14 days) gives this colt a live angle, and his consistent placed record across similar going is encouraging; his style is unclassified which adds an element of positional uncertainty, but his 7f to 8f form suggests the mile is within range.
runners_data.comment: Consistent in form throughout four outings, and open to improvement as the trip rises slightly today after appearing to want a more demanding test at Sandown last time; yet to score, but handles this going and the profile suggests more to come.

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's filly has shown she can place at this level and her prominent style puts her naturally close to the pace behind Hot And Cold; her soft-ground placed form slightly outnumbers her Good-to-Firm efforts, though she has run respectably on similar going before.
runners_data.comment: Just caught close home at Chepstow last time, going on well enough to suggest she is competitive at this level; effective at seven furlongs, though the quicker surface today is the main uncertainty for her.

runners_data.name: Legacy Rock
runners_data.note: Three wins in her last five starts at this trip mark her as the in-form runner, and the tongue tie is a retained piece of headgear she's won with; in truth she wants to race prominently but this field's pace dynamic has pushed her back toward midfield on the map — that positional compromise is worth factoring into expectation.
runners_data.comment: On a consistent upward curve with two wins in recent starts, but he raced freely and was worn down close home most recently on a mark 2lb lower than today's; first-time tongue-tie is applied, and his breeding suggests he may ultimately want further.

runners_data.name: Station Bar
runners_data.note: Won at Wolverhampton on Tapeta last time but her turf form on similar going (0W1P from three runs) is modest; she's a genuine hold-up horse who needs a genuinely run race to produce her finish, and this may not be the pace-shape that suits her.
runners_data.comment: Landed a handicap at Bath last time with a smooth passage through the field, but that came off a mark 5lb below today's; he handles the trip and ground, yet faces a stiffer task against better-rated rivals on these figures.

runners_data.name: John Harrison
runners_data.note: David Egan is a booking worth noting for Alan King, but 178 days off the track is a significant concern for this hold-up type; his single comparable-going run produced nothing and he has the widest price in the field for reason.
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in recent starts and returning from a 178-day absence, with his last run on the all-weather seeing him tire close home; he appears to have found his level, and the trainer's recent run of results is an added concern.

races.paceDynamic: Hot And Cold is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only Lyra Lea offering any prominent-position competition, she is likely to dictate from the front at a controlled, unchallenged tempo on this Good to Firm Salisbury mile. Legacy Rock is a genuinely prominent-minded horse who has been redistributed to a midfield slot on the map because Hot And Cold and Lyra Lea are ahead of her in the queue for that forward berth, meaning she may find herself racing slightly out of her natural position. The sustainable gallop that Hot And Cold sets up — unharassed and able to control fractions — typically favours horses with a turn of foot off a modest pace rather than pure grinders who need a stronger clip to close from the rear. This race shape most benefits prominent-to-midfield types with a finishing kick, as the hold-up horses Station Bar and John Harrison face the double penalty of conceding ground and having limited pace to aim at.

watchPoints.text: Hot And Cold has had 224 days off the track — watch her in the market and at the start; if she breaks poorly she loses her only natural advantage and the race opens up significantly.

Legacy Rock is a natural front-runner pressed into a midfield role by this field's shape — watch whether David Probert attempts to push forward regardless, which could inject unexpected early pace and unsettle Hot And Cold's rhythm.

The Good to Firm going report is consistent across all seven races at Salisbury today, suggesting a very fast surface — monitor whether this benefits the horse with the freshest legs (Hot And Cold) or exposes those with recent runs on softer ground such as Dark Sovereign and Lyra Lea.

Station Bar and John Harrison are both hold-up horses in a race with a single, unforced pace-setter — watch whether either jockey elects to creep closer than expected to avoid being left with too much to do in the Salisbury straight.
